**Hello, I’m [Your Name], a clinician who specializes in postpartum mental health.**  

I’d like to spend a few minutes with you today completing the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS)**. This short, 10‑item questionnaire is designed specifically to help us understand how you’ve been feeling over the past week since your baby arrived. It’s a routine part of postpartum care and can give us valuable insight into any mood or anxiety symptoms you might be experiencing.

Everything you share is completely confidential, and this is a safe, non‑judgmental space. My goal is simply to listen, learn about your experience, and make sure you have the support you need.

The EPDS consists of ten brief questions. I’ll ask them one at a time, and you can answer in the way that feels most accurate for you. There are no right or wrong answers—just what reflects your own feelings.

When you’re ready, we can begin.

**First question:**  
*In the past seven days, how often have you felt able to laugh and see the funny side of things?*
I’ve only been able to laugh or see the funny side of things a little bit—maybe only some of the time over the past week.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I’m glad you’re feeling that way. For me, it’s been harder to find those moments—I’ve only managed to laugh or see the humor in things a little bit, maybe just a few times this past week. It feels like most of the time I’m just going through the routine and the fatigue makes it tough to notice the lighter side.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things
It’s been only occasional for me. Some days I can feel a bit of enjoyment when something nice happens, but most of the time the interest just isn’t there and I don’t really look forward to things.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong
Yes, I do find myself blaming myself unnecessarily when something goes wrong, but it’s only occasional and not all the time. It’s just a mild feeling that pops up now and then.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason
Yes, I’ve felt anxious or worried for no good reason on occasion—mostly when I’m thinking about my baby’s health, but it’s not constant.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason
Yes, I’ve felt scared or panicky for no clear reason a few times this week—usually just a sudden rush of worry that passes fairly quickly, but it does happen on occasion.
Things have been getting on top of me
It’s been happening sometimes—I do feel like things are getting on top of me on a few days, especially when I’m exhausted from caring for the baby and trying to keep everything together.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping
I’ve been unhappy at times, and it’s made it harder to sleep on a few nights this week. It’s not every night, but I’ve definitely noticed the difficulty sleeping when I feel down.
I have felt sad or miserable
I’ve felt sad or miserable a few times this past week—more than never, but it’s not constant; it’s just occasional.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying
I’ve only cried a few times this past week—maybe once or twice when I felt especially overwhelmed. It’s not something that’s happening every day.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, I haven’t had any thoughts of harming myself.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 15: **Postpartum Depression/Anxiety Screening Summary**

**Client Identified Symptoms & Concerns**  
- **Mood:** Occasional sadness, feeling “unhappy,” occasional crying (1‑2 episodes/week).  
- **Anhedonia/Loss of Pleasure:** Limited enjoyment; looks forward to things only occasionally.  
- **Humor/Laughter:** Rarely able to laugh or see the funny side; mostly routine‑driven.  
- **Guilt/Self‑Blame:** Intermittent unnecessary self‑blame when things go wrong.  
- **Anxiety/Panic:** Occasional anxiety/worry (especially about infant health) and occasional brief panic‑type scares.  
- **Overwhelm/Stress:** Reports feeling “on top of me” on some days, particularly when exhausted.  
- **Sleep Disturbance:** Difficulty sleeping on a few nights, linked to low mood.  
- **Suicidal Ideation:** Denies any thoughts of self‑harm.

**Pattern Across Responses**  
- Predominantly **intermittent** rather than persistent symptoms.  
- Mood‑related symptoms (sadness, low enjoyment, crying) and anxiety symptoms are present **a few times per week**.  
- Sleep difficulty appears **situational**, coinciding with low mood episodes.  
- No continuous or severe functional impairment reported, but there is **notable difficulty coping** on days of high fatigue.

**Screening Significance (Postpartum Depression / Anxiety)**  
- **Low mood & anhedonia** – core features of postpartum depression.  
- **Crying spells** – may indicate worsening affective state.  
- **Sleep disruption** – common in postpartum mood disorders; linked here to mood.  
- **Guilt/self‑blame** – can exacerbate depressive symptomatology.  
- **Anxiety & occasional panic** – relevant for postpartum anxiety spectrum.  
- **Feeling overwhelmed** – suggests difficulty managing caregiving demands.  

**Risk Factors Noted**  
- Persistent (though intermittent) sadness and loss of pleasure.  
- Occasional crying episodes.  
- Sleep difficulties associated with mood changes.  
- Intermittent guilt/self‑blame.  
- Anxiety about infant health and occasional panic sensations.  
- **No suicidal ideation** reported (A10 = No).  

**Safety/Follow‑Up Recommendations**  
- Continue routine monitoring of mood, anxiety, sleep, and coping ability.  
- Re‑assess frequency/intensity of symptoms at next visit or sooner if symptoms intensify.  
- Provide patient with crisis resources and encourage immediate contact if suicidal thoughts emerge.  

*Prepared by: [Clinician Name], Licensed Mental Health Professional*  
*Date: 2025‑10‑07*
